programs.title: Lost Treasures of The Maya
programs.desc: Albert Lin spent many months in the Guatemalan jungle in the company of an international team of scientists.He recorded material at twelve major archaeological sites.The researchers had at their disposal a LiDAR device that works similarly to an X-ray.It allowed the terrain to be scanned from the air.Thanks to this, a digital map was developed.A special application was also created showing the local landscape without forests.Therefore, there was no need to cut down the trees.Objects that were part of previously unknown cities were found, including pyramids and a fortified citadel.They also found the skeleton of the queen, the ruler's burial chamber with richly decorated ritual vessels, fragments of the skull of a sacrificed child, bas-reliefs, a stone altar, a painted vase, as well as dozens of statuettes and ceramic objects.The discoveries made allowed us to re-evaluate the current knowledge about the Mayan civilization.

programs.title: Lost Treasures of the Bible
programs.sub_title: Secrets of the Tower of Babel
programs.desc: Researchers begin excavations in places associated with events described in the Bible.Their discoveries shed new light on the most famous stories from the Holy Bible.

programs.title: Goulag: Une histoire soviétique
programs.desc: Millions of people were sent to forced labor camps in the USSR, including many Poles.Often their fate remained unknown.Not only criminals were sent there, but also political opponents and citizens who offended the system.Cheap labor in mines, quarries and logging was to support the economy.All documents have not yet been declassified.Wiedzę o łagrach można czerpać między innymi z literatury - "Archipelagu Gułag" Aleksandra Sołżenicyna czy "Innego świata" Gustawa Herlinga-Grudzińskiego.

programs.title: Lost Ships of WW2
programs.desc: Just before the end of World War II, the cruiser USS Indianapolis sank after being torpedoed by a Japanese submarine.About 900 sailors found themselves in the open ocean.Hungry and cold, they fought for survival for five days.Some fell victim to sharks.Over 300 people were rescued.Books have been written about the disaster, documentaries have been made, and in 2016, the war drama "The Last Mission of the USS Indianapolis" with Nicolas Cage in the main role was premiered.This time, viewers will learn not only the shocking story of the survivors, but also the circumstances of finding the legendary wreck.Epilogue of war history To accurately present the fate of the cruiser and its crew, documentarians used archival film materials, computer animations, expert statements and moving accounts of miraculously survived sailors, including Edgar "Ed" Harrell.Thanks to this, viewers can feel the horror of the events of 1945.The wreck of the USS Indianapolis rested at the bottom of the Philippine Sea at a depth of over 5.5 km.Only 72 years after the tragedy, members of Paul Allen's expedition managed to locate it.Thanks to this, it was possible to write an epilogue to the story about the greatest maritime disaster in the history of the United States Navy.

programs.title: Air Crash Investigation
programs.desc: Behind the scenes of famous plane crashes.Viewers will see a reconstruction of the events that led to the tragedy.Fictionalized stories are complemented by accounts of pilots, experts, and witnesses..

programs.title: What Went Wrong
programs.desc: The creators of the series carefully analyze the causes of the great disasters of recent years and wonder whether they could have been avoided.These include the fire at London's Grenfell Tower.
